sentences.text:
This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C filed by the petitioners for quashing of FIR No.212/2018, under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Lahori Gate,
Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 28.12.2016 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
Thereafter, disputes and differences arose between them and they started living

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 09.12.2021 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, a revised settlement was entered into between the parties before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi on 07.07.2022 and as per the settlement, total amount of Rs. 1,80,000/- was paid by the petitioner no. 1 to the respondent no.2.
A copy of the said settlement is placed on record.
5. Petitioners are present through video conferencing and respondent no.2 is present in Court and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.

She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily,
without any force, pressure or coercion.

Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6.
Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.212/2018,
under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Lahori Gate, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 10:58:47 stand quashed.

However, the rights of the child born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains the majority as held by the Honble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh V. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors,
decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos. 4031-4032 of 2019.
8. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MAY 16, 2023/ib
